messages:
Maya (People Ops): quick heads up 1: leadership approved a limited exemption to the year-end blackout for specific on-call rotations.

Ethan (Eng-SRE): thank you! real question: does exemption grant extra PTO or just allow time off?

Maya (People Ops): exempted members can either: 1) keep scheduled days off during the blackout (manager approval required) OR 2) convert those days into 1 compensatory 'Comp Day' per blackout day taken, up to 3 days max. Comp Days go into a separate bucket valid for 6 months.

Ana (Manager): so if my engineer takes 2 blackout days while on rotation, I can approve 2 Comp Days instead of denying?

Maya (People Ops): correct. Manager must explicitly select 'approve and grant Comp Day' in the workflow.

Ethan (Eng-SRE): what about people who already swapped shifts and used PTO earlier this month? double-dipping?

Maya (People Ops): no double-dipping. If PTO was used and already approved, Comp Day won't be granted retroactively unless the manager marks the request as 'blackout exemption' and justifies it. We'll audit those on a case-by-case basis.

Ravi (Finance): payroll impact: Comp Days are not cashouts. They are time-off credits. If someone leaves before using Comp Days, there is no payout (per policy). Confirm legal ok?

Legal-Bot: noted. Standard separation language applies. Exceptions require legal sign-off; submit to legal@redwood.company for review.

Lena (Payroll): timeline: HR will publish exemption list by 2025-12-01. Managers must approve requests by 2025-12-18 to be reflected in year-end headcount reports. Comp Days will appear in payroll/time-off ledger on 2026-01-05.

Ana (Manager): can I pre-authorize the whole on-call rotation so my team doesn't need to file individual requests?

Maya (People Ops): managers can submit a single bulk request for an on-call cohort, but each person still needs an explicit line in the system (we'll pre-populate from your rotation schedule). Approval will be per-person but bulk UI will speed it.

Ethan (Eng-SRE): any change to accruals or carryover caps because of this?

Maya (People Ops): no change to standard carryover caps. Comp Days are outside carryover and expire after 6 months. If you convert a Wellness/PTO day into Comp Day, it counts toward the 3-day max and won't be added to carryover.

Ravi (Finance): we should flag managers with >5 approved Comp Days across orgs for review (cost/control). Can People Ops provide a weekly digest?

Maya (People Ops): yes, weekly digest to managers + finance starting 2025-12-05.

Lena (Payroll): process note: to ensure separation of duties, payroll will not auto-create Comp Days without a manager approval token. The token will be visible in the export.

Ethan (Eng-SRE): what about contractors who are on-call through vendor agreements?

Maya (People Ops): contractors are handled under their contract. Typically vendors get schedule flexibility, not Comp Days. If a contractor should be made eligible, escalate with legal and procurement.

Ana (Manager): are there blackout dates still enforced for teams outside on-call? I don't want people exploiting this for travel.

Maya (People Ops): blackout dates unchanged for general scheduling. This exemption is narrow: defined rotations with documented coverage. We will verify rosters against on-call schedules.

Ethan (Eng-SRE): cool. can you drop the request template?

timeoff-bot: Template published: https://intranet.redwood.company/timeoff/templates/oncall-blackout-exemption. Includes fields for rotation ID, coverage notes, manager justification.

Maya (People Ops): action items: 1) Managers: review rotation lists and submit bulk requests by 2025-12-10. 2) People Ops: publish FAQ and run one webinar (date TBA). 3) Payroll/Finance: confirm export fields.

Ravi (Finance): will run a dry-run export on 2025-12-12 and share with Maya/Lena.

Maya (People Ops): thanks everyone 1. We'll follow up in this channel with the FAQ. :wave:
